name: What Street Do You Like? Bogotá, Best of Three on Six Criteria
description:
Method replication: participants see sets of three Bogotá street views and pick the street that best answers each of six questions (most beautiful, safest, best to spend time in, best to live on, best to work or study, preferred to travel), 4 sets per question; the images are not the paper's stimuli (78 newly fetched Google Street View images spread across Bogotá, 2019 or later).

Original study: Guzman, Cantillo-Garcia, Criado, Sarmiento & Moncada (2026), Cities 168, 106460. In a stated-choice survey run face to face and online in Bogotá in January–May 2024 (2,659 responses), each participant saw four choice tasks of three panoramic Google Street View images, chosen with an orthogonal fractional design (Ngene, four blocks) from 12,285 images by the street attributes detected in them, and ranked them on the six criteria. Discrete choice models related colour, segmentation and object attributes to each criterion and produced a city-wide street preference index.

Differences from the original study: (1) images are drawn at random from the library instead of by the attribute-based experimental design; (2) participants pick the best street of each set instead of ranking all three, and each criterion gets its own sets; (3) background questions cover sex, education and socioeconomic stratum only, not occupation, household size, zone of residence or income.
author: Guzman, Cantillo-Garcia, Criado, Sarmiento & Moncada
